propositions: Six proposed deterministic clarity criteria reject valid historical tickets that passed plan-review and completion-verifier attestation.
Required canonical sections can be disproved by tickets using semantic aliases or compact plans where mechanism resides in What or AC rather than Approach/Scope headings.
Placeholder lexicon detection (e.g., 'check if') produces false positives on mechanically decidable conditionals with fully specified actions.
Hard per-AC explicit proof-coverage markers are unnecessary when behavioral assertions are precise; many valid tickets lack 'verified by' sentinels.
Edit-set requirements fail for read-only analysis, operational, and external-attestation work with explicit no-edit output contracts.
AC conjunction counts cannot distinguish bundled independent deliverables from one coherent matrix; deterministic counts are unsound for vague/hedge detection.
